identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log — Forklift FL-2 (Toyota 8FGU25), September 2026, Portland Warehouse

scan.summary: This is an internal daily inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse, tracking the pre-shift checklist required under 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). It shows entries from September 1 through September 18, 2026, records one horn defect, and lists two certified operators with their next evaluation due dates. As a record, it is judged on completeness and recency rather than against a written standard.
scan.freshness_note: The log's last dated entry is September 18, 2026 — nine days before today (September 27, 2026). It has not been continued through the current date, which is itself a completeness gap for a daily-use record.

gaps.title: Missing inspection entries for days the truck was operated
gaps.description: There are no entries for September 3 and 4, 2026, but the hour meter rose from 4,819 (Sep 2) to 4,834 (Sep 7) — a 15-hour increase — showing the truck was run on the missing days without a documented pre-shift check.
gaps.fix: Investigate and document why no inspection was recorded for the days the meter shows operation; going forward, ensure a pre-shift inspection entry is made every day the truck is used, with no exceptions.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7); enforced in Oregon via OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect noted with no corrective-action record
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn is marked defective with the note 'Horn not working,' but the very next operating day (Sep 10) the horn is marked OK with no note of repair, replacement, or removal from service in between.
gaps.fix: Add a corrective-action entry showing the defect was reported, the truck taken out of service until repaired, and the repair date/who performed it, before returning the horn status to OK.

gaps.title: Log not continued through the current date
gaps.description: The log's last entry is Sep 18, 2026; there are no entries for Sep 19 through Sep 27 (today), a gap of roughly nine operating days with no pre-shift inspection record.
gaps.fix: Resume daily pre-shift entries immediately and backfill or explain the gap for Sep 19–27 if the truck was used during that period.

gaps.title: Supervisor review not completed
gaps.description: The supervisor review line at the bottom of the log is blank — no signature and no date entered — so the month's entries have not been reviewed or signed off by a supervisor.
gaps.fix: Have the responsible supervisor review the completed log and sign and date the review line.
gaps.citation: Not tied to a specific OSHA provision; a documentation-completeness practice rather than a cited rule

facts.value: No inspection entries exist for Sep 3–4, 2026, despite hour-meter evidence the truck was operated on those days
facts.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.
facts.affects: Shows the log is incomplete for days the truck was actually in use, undermining the record's value as proof of daily pre-shift inspection.

expected_missing.title: Written Powered Industrial Truck Safety Program / operator training program
expected_missing.why: Companies operating forklifts typically hold a written program describing training, evaluation, and refresher-training procedures that this log's operator due-dates presumably flow from.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Forklift maintenance/repair log
expected_missing.why: A separate maintenance record showing when the horn (and other flagged defects) were actually repaired would normally accompany a pre-shift inspection log.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Inspection logs for any other powered industrial trucks on site
expected_missing.why: If the Portland warehouse operates more than one truck, similar companies keep one log per unit; only FL-2's log was provided here.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the direct quotes and the missing/last-entry dates, which are read straight from the table. The citation to 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) and Oregon's adoption via OAR 437-002-0220 is well established and consistent with the earlier open findings on this same log. Lower confidence on whether the operator evaluation due dates recur on a fixed cycle versus being one-time dates, though the three-year interval matches the general OSHA reevaluation practice under 1910.178(l)(4)(iii). The supervisor-review gap is a completeness practice, not a specific cited OSHA requirement, as already noted in the open finding.
